content: Co-trimoxazole is a combination antibiotic containing trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole, which is classified as a sulfa drug. It works by eradicating bacteria responsible for various infections, including those affecting the urinary tract, lungs (such as pneumonia), ears, and intestines. Additionally, it is used to treat traveler's diarrhea. It is important to note that antibiotics like co-trimoxazole are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Co-trimoxazole is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken twice daily, but in cases of severe lung infections, it may be prescribed up to four times a day. Each dose should be accompanied by a full glass of water. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take co-trimoxazole exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless advised by your doctor. Before starting co-trimoxazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, diuretics (water pills), oral diabetes medications, any sulfa drugs, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially methotrexate, phenytoin (Dilantin), warfarin (Coumadin), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease, asthma, severe allergies, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency, which is an inherited blood disorder. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking co-trimoxazole, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as this medication may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Co-trimoxazole may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Co-trimoxazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, vomiting, or loss of appetite. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash, itching, sore throat, fever or chills, mouth sores, unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, paleness, or joint aches. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain lab tests may be ordered to monitor your response to co-trimoxazole. Do not share this medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of co-trimoxazole, contact your doctor.
